validation.description:
Where and how to drive the target application's GUI.

``kind`` selects the concrete :class:`~openadapt_flow.backend.Backend` the
CLI drives (built by :func:`openadapt_flow.backends.factory.build_backend`):

- ``web`` (default) — the Playwright/Chromium browser backend. Reproduces
  the historical behavior exactly (``url`` / ``headed`` are browser fields);
  every other field here is ignored.
- ``windows`` — the WAA (Windows Agent Arena) HTTP backend for native
  Windows desktops. Requires ``agent_url`` (the in-guest agent's base URL);
  ``agent_token`` authenticates a token-protected agent.
- ``macos`` — a local native macOS application window. Requires
  ``macos_app``; ``macos_window_title`` should uniquely identify the target
  window when the application owns more than one.
- ``linux`` — one exact local Linux application window through AT-SPI.
  Requires ``linux_app`` and ``linux_window_title``. Native accessibility
  actions are preferred; global pointer/keyboard fallback is opt-in.
- ``rdp`` — a pixel-only network-RDP or local remote-display backend.
  ``rdp_host`` drives a network RDP session (FreeRDP/aardwolf);
  ``rdp_window`` instead drives a local remote-display client window.
- ``citrix`` — the local Citrix Workspace/Viewer window preset over the
  remote-display backend. It defaults the owner selector for the host OS,
  accepts ``rdp_window`` / ``rdp_window_title`` overrides, and refuses an
  ``rdp_host`` rather than silently constructing the wrong RDP substrate.

Every non-``web`` field is optional and defaults to None, so an existing
``web`` deployment (or an empty config) is byte-for-byte unchanged.
validation.title: BackendConfig

AuthRef.description:
A reference to an HTTP credential held OUTSIDE the config.

Exactly one auth style may be set:

- ``bearer_env`` -- name of an env var holding a bearer token; resolves to
  ``Authorization: Bearer <token>``.
- ``header`` + ``value_env`` -- an arbitrary auth header (e.g.
  ``X-API-Key``) whose VALUE comes from the named env var. Token-pair
  ``Authorization: token <key>:<secret>`` fits here too (put the whole
  value in the env var).
- ``basic_env`` -- name of an env var holding ``user:password``; resolves
  to ``Authorization: Basic <base64>``.

No field ever holds the secret itself -- only the env var NAME.

EffectsConfig.description:
Which system of record to verify consequential writes against.

``kind`` selects the concrete
:class:`~openadapt_flow.runtime.effects.EffectVerifier`. ``none`` (default)
wires no verifier — a bundle that declares NO effects then replays exactly
as before, but a step that DOES declare effects HALTs (fail-safe: an
unverifiable consequential write is never silently accepted).

Effect-verifier kit conventions (``docs/EFFECT_KIT.md``):

- **Secrets are references, never literals.** ``auth`` /
  ``access_token_env`` / ``sql_password_env`` name environment variables
  staged by the operator; a missing variable fails LOUD at construction.
- **Run-parameter binding is explicit.** Every ``*_params`` /
  ``*_exprs`` mapping takes the same ``{param: name}`` / ``{literal: v}``
  :class:`~openadapt_flow.runtime.effects.ValueExpr` form bundles use (a
  bare string is a literal), and is resolved against the governed run
  parameters (``--params-file`` / ``--param``) when the verifier is
  BUILT — so one bundle + one deployment YAML ships with its verification
  bound to the record each run actually writes.
EffectsConfig.title: EffectsConfig

FieldReader.description:
How to read one value from the record page.

``selector`` is a CSS selector relative to the row (or to the page, for
the identity check). An empty selector reads the row element itself.
``attribute`` reads that attribute instead of the rendered text, which is
how a page that shortens long text can still expose the full value (for
example a ``title`` attribute).
FieldReader.title: FieldReader

FileSource.description: A file on this computer: its contents and SHA-256.
FileSource.title: FileSource

FinalCheck.description: Make the first read provisional and settle it with a later read.
FinalCheck.title: FinalCheck

FrameAttribution.description:
Where the judge learns who changed a record.

``audit_read``: a second read-only read (``read``, the same shape as an
``effects:`` verifier section) returns the app's audit log or change
feed. Entries present after the save and not before are the window's
entries. ``record_field`` names the entry field that refers to a record
(compared with :attr:`FrameSpec.identity_field`), ``actor_field`` the
user or session.

``record_field`` attribution: each record carries its last modifier in
``actor_field`` and, optionally, a version or ETag in ``version_field``.
A changed record whose version did not move is unattributed.
FrameAttribution.title: FrameAttribution

FrameDatabase.description:
``frame.database``: diff the whole database, not only what is read.

Every table and column is snapshotted before and after the save
(``db_snapshot.py``), and each table is judged as one more slice: a row
added, removed or changed is collateral unless a declared effect, a
declared side record or an attributed concurrent writer explains it. A
new declared or side row that sets a column the effects don't name, and
that ``new_row_fields`` doesn't list, is collateral too.

``allow_tables`` replaces a read-list with a reviewed allow-list: the
tables the app writes on its own for any signed-in user (logs, sessions,
id registries). They are append-only unless an entry says ``skip`` with a
reason. Everything else is compared. The receipt counts tables compared,
append-only and skipped, and binds the list's digest.
FrameDatabase.title: FrameDatabase

GroundingModelConfig.description:
Operator-selected ("bring your own") model-grounding endpoint.

The last rung of the resolution ladder is a Grounder that PROPOSES a click
point when the deterministic rungs abstain. This section lets a deployment
point that fallback rung at a model of its choice instead of the built-in
Anthropic default: a self-hosted vLLM/Ollama, an OpenRouter/Azure/Bedrock
proxy, or the Anthropic API directly.

Two hard invariants:

* **Configuring a model NEVER enables egress by itself.** This section only
  names WHICH model would be used; whether ANYTHING leaves the box is still
  governed entirely by ``allow_model_grounding`` (default False => fully
  local). An enabled model with egress off stays dormant.
* **The API key is a reference, never a literal.** ``api_key_env`` names the
  environment variable holding the key; the key itself is never stored in
  the config or in the repository.

Fail-safe: the constructed grounder only ever proposes a point; the identity
band and risk gate still dispose before any click, and any endpoint error
yields no proposal (the ladder halts).
GroundingModelConfig.title: GroundingModelConfig

Declares that this deployment drives a resettable test copy.

Only ``induce --probe-on`` reads it. Probing replays guessed

purpose, so it runs only where the operator has said in writing that the

RdpSession.description: A second RDP session, signed in as a separate account.

ReadbackNav.description:
One deterministic navigation action to RE-OPEN the written record by a
path DIFFERENT from the write flow, before an on-screen read-back.

Auto-derived from the demonstration (the steps the person took to view the
saved record again — e.g. clear the form, search the patient, open the
encounter). Deliberately tiny and model-free: a re-navigation is replayed
by coordinate/keyboard exactly as recorded; anything a backend cannot
perform makes the read-back INDETERMINATE (HALT), never a guessed CONFIRM.
ReadbackNav.title: ReadbackNav

RecordIdentity.description: The check that the page shows the record the session asked for.
RecordIdentity.title: RecordIdentity

ReferenceCapture.description:
Read the saved record's identifier from the run's own session.

Some applications only issue the identifier at the save: a claim number,
a submission reference, a confirmation number. Right after the save the
verifier reads it once, here, and opens the record page by it in the
separate session. ``source`` is ``"url"`` (the page URL the run's session
shows, from a backend that exposes ``url``) or ``"screen"`` (local OCR of
the run's current screenshot, optionally limited to ``region``).
``pattern`` is a regular expression with exactly one capture group; it
must match exactly one distinct value, or the check is INDETERMINATE.
ReferenceCapture.title: ReferenceCapture

RemoteFrameContract.description: Reviewed exact-geometry exclusions for derived settle inputs only.
RemoteFrameContract.title: RemoteFrameContract

RemoteHumanDecisionConfig.description:
Explicit remote attended-decision issuance policy.

This section does not configure a network provider and does not grant
execution authority.  It permits a customer-controlled runner to project
the current signed pause as a PHI-free AAL2 task for its configured control
plane.  The engine-owned pause capability and fresh live revalidation stay
authoritative when a decision returns.
RemoteHumanDecisionConfig.title: RemoteHumanDecisionConfig

RepairSection.description:
Automatic repair of stops that wrote nothing (docs/SELF_REPAIR.md).

When ``agent`` is set, every ``run`` that halts before any effect hands
the stop to this repair agent, probes its fix up to the save, asks one
person (or applies a pre-approved standard change), and resumes. A stop
after a write is never repaired. ``auto: false`` or ``--no-auto-repair``
turns it off. Omitted when serialized at its defaults.
RepairSection.title: RepairSection

RepairSessionSpec.description:
How self-repair opens a fresh app session outside a browser.

A probe, each fault probe and the resumed run each need the app freshly
started; the halted session stays as it is. Each command is an argv run
on the machine Flow runs on, with no shell. It must keep running while the
app is up and own (it, or a process of its group) the one window
``backend:`` binds to; Flow checks that, and ends the group afterwards. A
backend whose window is not on this machine (Windows over its agent,
FreeRDP) can't show that, so repair there is refused for now.
RepairSessionSpec.title: RepairSessionSpec

ReportFormat.description: How to read one kind of report.
ReportFormat.title: ReportFormat

RollbackSection.description:
Compensating rollback after a stop (docs/ROLLBACK.md).

Off unless ``enabled``. When on, the run reads the system of record before
it starts; after a stop it runs the compensation a person approved for
each change, latest first, and reads the store again. It is
``ROLLED_BACK`` only when that read matches the first one.
RollbackSection.title: RollbackSection

RuntimeSection.description: Runtime posture: durability and model-egress opt-in.

SearchStep.description: Find the record: type ``query`` into ``box`` and submit.

SmartBackendConfig.description:
``effects.smart_backend`` in ``deployment.yaml`` or ``verify.yaml``.

Exactly one key source: ``private_key_file``, ``private_key_env`` or
``jwks_file``. ``kid`` is required for a PEM key; for a JWKS it selects the
key and defaults to the only private key in the set.
SmartBackendConfig.title: SmartBackendConfig

ValueExpr.description:
A single effect-contract value: either a static ``literal`` or a
reference to a run ``param`` (P0-3 fix).

Before this type an :class:`Effect` carried plain static strings, so a
PARAMETERIZED workflow verified its effects against the values baked in at
DEMONSTRATION time (write patient "Susan" via the GUI, then verify the
recorded demo patient "Phil"). ``ValueExpr`` lets a compiled effect declare
``{"param": "patient_id"}`` and have the runtime resolve it against the
RUN's params before verification, so the record actually written is the
record checked.

Exactly one of :attr:`literal` / :attr:`param` is meaningful. Old bundles
(and hand-authored effects) that pass a bare string are coerced to
``ValueExpr(literal=...)`` by :class:`Effect`'s validators, and this type's
``__eq__`` / ``__str__`` compare/render as that bare string so every
existing reader (learning gate signatures, codegen review comments) and the
substrate matchers behave BYTE-FOR-BYTE identically for a literal.
ValueExpr.title: ValueExpr

WindowsRegistrySource.description: One value in the Windows registry.

RepairSessionSpec.description:
How self-repair opens a fresh app session outside a browser.

A probe, each fault probe and the resumed run each need the app freshly
started; the halted session stays as it is. Each command is an argv run
on the machine Flow runs on, with no shell. It must keep running while the
app is up and own (it, or a process of its group) the one window
``backend:`` binds to; Flow checks that, and ends the group afterwards. A
backend whose window is not on this machine (Windows over its agent,
FreeRDP) can't show that, so repair there is refused for now.
RepairSessionSpec.title: RepairSessionSpec

validation.description:
Automatic repair of stops that wrote nothing (docs/SELF_REPAIR.md).

When ``agent`` is set, every ``run`` that halts before any effect hands
the stop to this repair agent, probes its fix up to the save, asks one
person (or applies a pre-approved standard change), and resumes. A stop
after a write is never repaired. ``auto: false`` or ``--no-auto-repair``
turns it off. Omitted when serialized at its defaults.
validation.title: RepairSection

FrameAttribution.description:
Where the judge learns who changed a record.

``audit_read``: a second read-only read (``read``, the same shape as an
``effects:`` verifier section) returns the app's audit log or change
feed. Entries present after the save and not before are the window's
entries. ``record_field`` names the entry field that refers to a record
(compared with :attr:`FrameSpec.identity_field`), ``actor_field`` the
user or session.

``record_field`` attribution: each record carries its last modifier in
``actor_field`` and, optionally, a version or ETag in ``version_field``.
A changed record whose version did not move is unattributed.
FrameAttribution.title: FrameAttribution

FrameDatabase.description:
``frame.database``: diff the whole database, not only what is read.

Every table and column is snapshotted before and after the save
(``db_snapshot.py``), and each table is judged as one more slice: a row
added, removed or changed is collateral unless a declared effect, a
declared side record or an attributed concurrent writer explains it. A
new declared or side row that sets a column the effects don't name, and
that ``new_row_fields`` doesn't list, is collateral too.

``allow_tables`` replaces a read-list with a reviewed allow-list: the
tables the app writes on its own for any signed-in user (logs, sessions,
id registries). They are append-only unless an entry says ``skip`` with a
reason. Everything else is compared. The receipt counts tables compared,
append-only and skipped, and binds the list's digest.
FrameDatabase.title: FrameDatabase
